meta.notes: Story-mode steps; bodies are templated at export time from the exported numbers. Each selector starts with the data-story attribute the screen renders (story_id), optionally narrowed to a child element so the step card does not cover its subject: aog-incident-ps1, aircraft, rotable-float-calc, network-bom, action-inbox, frontier-chart. mobile_selector (or null) is the narrower target used at <= 480 px (bottom-sheet layout); it also starts with the story_id hook. title_simple / body_simple are the Simple-mode (plain English) text, computed from the same numbers; title / body are the Expert text.

steps.title: 1 · The operational problem
steps.body: A6-FHW (fictional) is grounded at BOM: a D0 nose wheel steering actuator (NB) failed with none held there. The part arrived at 9 h; release came at 14 h. Best route on what the desk knew then: Transfer from AUH.
steps.body_simple: A plane is stuck at Mumbai. A part it needs before its next flight broke, and no spare was kept there. The part arrived after 9 hours, and the plane flew again after 14 hours.

steps.title: 2 · Diagnose the shortage
steps.body: ATA 32 rates URGENT, led by GN-32-R014 (D0 nose wheel steering actuator (NB)), risk 100/100. With 0 units at BOM under the Simple Rulebook, it caused 464 AOG h across all stations in W52–W103.
steps.body_simple: The landing gear group is the biggest risk, and one part leads it. With no spare at Mumbai, it kept planes grounded for 464 hours across all airports in the last year.

steps.title: 3 · The repair pipeline
steps.body: Pooled over the 72-day repair loop, the Network Plan's 17 spares cover over 99.9% of removals. At BOM the Network Plan holds 2 units (Simple Rulebook: 0), refilled from AUH in 4.3 days: 99.7% of D0 needs find one on the shelf.
steps.body_simple: Broken parts spend about 72 days in repair, so the airline needs spares to cover them. The Network Plan keeps 17 in total, so one is almost always on the shelf. At Mumbai it keeps 2, refilled from Abu Dhabi in about 4 days.

steps.title: 4 · Compare the trade-offs
steps.body: In this simulation, across 120 modelled part numbers: at BOM, holdout material AOG falls from 242 h/yr (Simple Rulebook) to 6 (Network Plan, 11 rotables here). Network Plan + Extra Spares takes network AOG to 76 h/yr.
steps.body_simple: In this simulation, planes at Mumbai were grounded 242 hours a year under the Simple Rulebook, and 6 under the Network Plan. Across all 120 modelled part numbers, the Network Plan + Extra Spares brings the network total to 76 hours a year.

steps.title: 5 · Recommend the action
steps.body: The action centre raises 63 exceptions for W103, 25 urgent. At BOM, GN-32-R014 has 0 of 2 on hand, with 7 D0 requests and 75 AOG h there in the last 52 weeks (W52–W103). Action: Position 2 units at BOM (station target 0 -> 2).
steps.body_simple: The planner's list has 63 alerts this week, 25 of them urgent. Mumbai has 0 of the 2 spares it should hold for this part. The advice is to send 2 there.

steps.title: 6 · Business value on the Readiness Frontier
steps.body: In this simulation, across 120 modelled part numbers, the Network Plan cuts material AOG by 1,480 h a year vs the Simple Rulebook. It buys 68 rotables (≈AED 8.4M) and removes 20 (≈AED 3.1M); average simulated inventory +AED 0.6M.
steps.body_simple: In this simulation, across 120 modelled part numbers, the Network Plan cuts grounded time by 1,480 hours a year. It buys 68 repairable spares (about AED 8.4M) and removes 20 (about AED 3.1M), so stock value rises by about AED 0.6M.
